## Summary
<!-- Provide detailed PR description below -->
Add the ability to allow skipping binding passkey on both new user registration and the next sign-in attempt.
- When skipping on new registration: The status is only saved in the current interaction session.
- When skipping on sign-in: The status is persisted in DB and thus will not prompt again on next sign-in.

comments.body: better add some comments explaining "what" will be skipped

Can we use a single API with optional parameters to indicate whether to persist the skipped status in the DB?  Or maybe simply avoid introducing new parameters, and simply check the interaction event when submitting the interaction.

Similarly, using a shared property like `skipPasskeyBinding` might be sufficient. When submitting the interaction, we can read this property and persist it to the database if the `interactionEvent` is signIn. This avoids introducing additional fields and keeps the skip binding behavior centralized in the interaction session as a single source of truth.

P.S. since the logic was implemented in the `mfa` class. Maybe a more accurate name is prefered like `passkeySignInBinding`, this will avoid confusion between mfaSkipped (WebAuthn binding ) vs passKey skipped.
ditto: using passkeySignIn instead of passkey to avoid `WebAuthn` vs `Passkey` confusion
We can, but this is following the existing MFA API design patterns.
